title: Hole in the Wall
summary: Fit a robot whose corners are matrix columns through a hole: equal entries, row-by-column products, rotations and the order of two machines.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Matrix products depend on the order
learningOutcome: The student can match entries of equal matrices to find unknowns, compute a row-by-column product, read a rotation matrix, and see that AB and BA differ.

levels.title: Match the entries
levels.adds: Baseline: two matrices are equal when every matching entry is equal, so each letter comes from one entry (Ex 3.1 Q6, Q7, Q9).
hints: Compare the two matrices entry by entry, top left first.
An entry with only x in it tells you x. An entry with only y tells you y.
Check the last entries: they must agree with your x and y.

levels.title: The machine A
levels.adds: New: the entry in row i, column j of A·P is row i of A times column j of P, with unknowns inside A (Ex 3.2 Q1, Q3, Q9 to Q12).
hints: Row 1 of A times column 1 of P gives the top left entry of the result.
Write that entry as an equation with a, then solve it.
Do the same for the second row with b.

levels.title: The turntable
levels.adds: New: the rotation matrix with cos α and sin α; read cos α and sin α from where a corner lands (Ex 3.2 Q2, Q6, Q13; Ex 3.3 Q12).
hints: A corner at (2, 0) lands at (2 cos α, 2 sin α).
Halve the landing coordinates to get cos α and sin α.
Use the special angles π/6, π/4 and π/3, and watch the signs.

levels.title: Two machines, two orders
levels.adds: New: matrix products depend on the order, so AB ≠ BA; choose the order as well as the shear (Ex 3.2 Q14; Examples 13 to 15).
hints: Work out BAP and ABP for a small k and compare them with the hole.
Look at one entry that changes with k in only one of the two orders.

misconceptions: AB = BA for any two matrices
A matrix product multiplies entry by matching entry
A rotation matrix has the same entry everywhere
